final_message:
Blog post URLs now keep the base letter of accented characters: "Crème brûlée recipes" becomes `creme-brulee-recipes`. `npm test` passes all 3 tests, including `test/blog-slug.test.js`.

The bug was in `vendor/slugify`, which deletes every non-ASCII character before slugifying. I didn't touch `vendor/`. The fix is in `src/blog/slug.js`: it splits accents off their letters (NFD form), drops the accent marks, and then calls the vendored function. I left a short comment explaining why.

Shop URLs still have the same problem. `src/shop/product-url.js` calls the same vendored `slugify` directly, so "Crème brûlée" there still becomes `crme-brle`. I didn't change it because you asked about blog posts. The same normalize step would fix it, and I can apply it if you want. The permanent fix belongs in the vendored library, which the platform team upgrades.
